The toolbox builds a Wflow-SBM model from global data, generates weather across a scenario-neutral
temperature × precipitation grid and calculates indicators from retained responses.
CMIP6 changes provide plausibility context; they do not select or weight the tested grid.
Outputs support screening, not an automatically calibrated basin model or a decision by the software.

## Start here

1. [Install](guide/install.qmd) and check external-data access.
2. [Run the example](guide/quick-start.md) and find its output tables.
3. Use the [own-case guide](guide/new-case.qmd) and
   [indicator guide](guide/indicators.qmd) for your assessment choices.
4. [Run/resume](guide/running.md), [read outputs](guide/outputs.md) and check qualifications.

The [technical manual](technical-manual/overview.qmd) describes implemented interfaces.
The existing [scientific approach](scientific-approach/overview.qmd) explains assessment rationale and limits.
The manuals cover table interpretation, selection and extension. A supported response-surface construction
walkthrough is not yet available. Use [Downloads](downloads.qmd) for complete HTML and PDF volumes;
the technical manual includes the module contract and all five indicator-set references.

## The five workflows

WF0 compares historical climate and can run alone for forcing selection.
WF1 builds the historical model; WF3 independently generates climate series. Both supply WF4 simulation
and indicator calculation. WF2 is optional projection context and never drives WF3.
The runner executes enabled workflows in WF0 → WF1 → WF2 → WF3 → WF4 order.
